why: Copy routing is a STATIC CIRCUIT per lane pair, not a destination field: the lane tile link layer (ot_s81ph_link_ep seq/CRC/go-back-N/credits, FROZEN HF-3) is end-to-end per peer pair across the switch (rtl/dsrom_sys/s81_dv/slice/ot_s81sl_slice_lep.sv header (c); results/arch/mu_s81_1018/chain_plan.json form). One copy = one extra lane pair on every pre-group TX and post-group RX rank die.

The multi-user endpoint is hard 2-way: ot_s81sl_lep_core AB_EN gives NL = 4 lanes (pair A lanes 0/1, pair B lanes 2/3); the copy select is ONE bit (mu_c[1] -> w_ab; ab_ok forces user 0 to A). x3/x4 have no encoding and no lanes 4..7.

Hence x4 on L2/8/14/20 needs: (1) endpoint RTL with a 2-bit copy field, 8 lanes, 4-way TX select and 4-way RX merge (the 2-way pair-B RX merge already missed setup by 575 ps before the MU-S81-2/RX redesign); (2) mu_c command / seq_host calendar word change; (3) +2 SerDes lane pairs (4 PHY lanes, 4 more dsfd_coll_lane tiles, ~+4.4k face pins) on each of the 4 rank dies of the 4 pre-group and 4 post-group stages = 32 dies of a new p4l die master, new hardened lepmu kit + parent + die GEN/GRT/STA. dsplit makes the post-group (receiving) stage gather from 4 copies, same RX change.
Relay-tree alternative (copy A forwards to C) also needs AB endpoints on both faces of the copy dies (new die master) and holds copy A stage/links for C users: physical change + calendar violation.
Today the 2-way endpoint itself is still closing (DRIVE-S81-LEPMU / LEPENHMU gating 10-20): closure risk even before x4.

bandwidth.note: bandwidth is NOT the limiter; ports/endpoints are

l1_x2: L1 x2 alone fits the existing AB endpoint (die-count + mab die variant instances only), but it is only useful with dsplit + x4.
decision: Ship 141 stages / 648 dies (48 AR users x 1,010.1 = 48,486 tok/s, 74.8/die). B/C/D (dsplit compiler/allocator, x4 calendar) NOT started per the decision rule.
